title: Resolve gated actions when no human is at a screen
description:
Purpose: reconcile requirement 3 (work continues when the laptop is closed) with requirement 4 (consequential actions are gated) before any approval code is specified.

v1 is a web tab. Device push is "come back, something finished," not "approve this now" (docs/MESSAGING.md). iOS is v3. So a consequential action that a routine or an overnight turn reaches while nobody is at a screen has no completable approval path.

Either overnight work is scoped to non-consequential actions (the honest v1, matching the first-handoff example: draft overnight, approve in the morning), or auto-review gets loosened so routines finish unattended and the threat model becomes theatre. The third option — silent failure or indefinite blocking — is the failure mode this epic exists to prevent.

Definition of Done:
- The v1 scope of "work continues with the laptop closed" is written explicitly: which consequential classes may run unattended, and which may not.
- For each consequential class that may run unattended, an enforceable control (structured connector, pre-authorized rule, or human takeover) is named, or the class is excluded from overnight work.
- No approval design depends on a human being present at a screen unless that presence is guaranteed.
- The decision is recorded in the approval spec and in docs/ROADMAP.md, not discovered in production.

Not included: the full iOS/push approval client (v3), routine scheduling mechanics (v2).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Decision recorded in docs/APPROVAL.md and docs/ROADMAP.md item 7. Unattended consequential classes run only against a human always-allow that binds exact structured arguments; generic authenticated browser cannot be pre-authorized overnight. Kernel: overnight_gated_action, exact_consequential_approval, unsupported_browser_action. Not on live ThinTurn HTTP loop. No staging/production deploy.
